---
title: "Glossary"
---

Plain-English definitions of the terms used in these two days.

## R and programming

**Object**: anything with a name in R. A number, a dataset, a plot, a model.

**Vector**: a sequence of values of the same type. A column of your data.

**Data frame / tibble**: a rectangle. Rows are observations, columns are
variables. A tibble is a data frame with better printing.

**Function**: a verb. Takes arguments in brackets, returns something.

**Argument**: an input to a function. `round(x, digits = 2)` has two.

**Package**: a bundle of functions someone else wrote. Install once, load
each session with `library()`.

**Pipe (`|>`)**: passes the result on the left into the function on the
right. Makes multi-step code read in the order it happens.

**Chunk**: a block of code inside a Quarto document, fenced by ```` ```{r} ````.

**Working directory**: the folder R considers "here". Set by opening a
project; never by `setwd()`.

**Project (`.Rproj`)**: a folder RStudio treats as the root of the world.

**Environment**: the objects that currently exist in memory. Emptied by
restarting R, which is a feature.

**`NA`**: a missing value. Not zero, not empty text. Arithmetic on `NA`
gives `NA`, deliberately.

**Factor**: a categorical variable with a fixed set of levels and an order
you can control.

## Reproducibility

**Reproducibility**: same data + same code → same result.

**Replicability**: new data, same method → same conclusion.

**Generalisability**: the finding holds beyond the setting studied.

**Literate programming**: code and prose in one document, so the report is
generated by the analysis rather than describing it.

**Dynamic document**: a document whose numbers are computed at render time.

**Version control (git)**: a record of every change, who made it and why.

**Provenance**: the traceable path from raw data to published number.

## Quarto

**YAML**: the metadata block between `---` fences at the top of a `.qmd`.

**Markdown**: plain-text formatting. `**bold**`, `## heading`.

**Render**: run the code and produce the output document.

**Chunk option**: a `#|` line controlling one chunk's behaviour.

**Inline code**: `` `r expression` `` inside prose. How numbers stay correct.

**Cross-reference**: `@fig-gain`, automatically numbered and linked.

**CSL**: Citation Style Language, the file that formats your references.

**Shortcode**: a `{{{< >}}}` directive expanded at render time.

**Freeze**: caching, so unchanged chunks are not re-run on every render.

## Statistics and study design

**Confounding**: a third variable driving both exposure and outcome.

**Baseline comparability**: whether the groups were similar before the
intervention. Check it before interpreting any difference after.

**Complete-case analysis**: analysing only rows with no missing values.
What `na.rm = TRUE` silently gives you.

**Effect size**: how big the difference is. A p-value does not tell you.

**Multiple comparisons**: testing many hypotheses inflates false positives.

**Pre-specification**: deciding the analysis before seeing the results.

## AI

**Large language model (LLM)**: a model that predicts the next token.
Optimised for plausibility, not truth.

**Prompt**: what you type. Context + task + constraints + format.

**Hallucination**: fluent, confident, false output. Citations and function
arguments are the usual victims.

**Token**: the unit an LLM reads and writes; roughly a word fragment.

**Disclosure**: the statement in your manuscript naming which tool did
what. Required by ICMJE.
